note: Plan items and summary for the adult oncology demo. Says only what was said in the visit; gaps become questions.

plan_items.text: Chemotherapy called FOLFOX, every two weeks for about three to six months, starting in two weeks.
A nurse navigator named Maria will call this week.

summary:
You had surgery for colon cancer. The lab found cancer cells in 3 of 14 lymph nodes. This is called stage three.

Your plan:
1. Chemotherapy called FOLFOX. It lowers the chance the cancer comes back.
2. Every two weeks for about three to six months.
3. It starts in two weeks. Blood is drawn first.
4. A nurse named Maria will call you this week.

Common side effects: feeling sick, feeling tired, and numb or tingling hands and feet, most in the cold. You will get medicine for the sick feeling.

Questions to ask your team:
- Which signs mean I call you, and what number do I use at night?
- Does a pump go home with me, and for how long?
- My chart says I have nerve trouble in my feet. Does that matter with this chemo?
- Is blood thinner medicine on my chart? Does it matter with chemo?
- Can I keep working?
- Are there other options?
